hints: The input asks for the kth ancestor of a node, with k potentially large.
Precompute each node's 2^j-th ancestor from two 2^(j-1) jumps.
Decompose k into powers of two and lift the node for each set bit.
analogy: Climb a huge number of manager links in jumps of 1,2,4,8,... steps.
example: If k=5=4+1, jump four ancestors and then one more.
correctness: The table entries are exact compositions of parent links, and every k is a sum of powers of two, so the selected jumps reach the kth ancestor.
complexity: O(n log n+q log n) time and O(n log n) space.
algorithm: Root the company tree at employee 1 and precompute binary ancestors up[j][v], the 2^j-th manager of v. For query (v,k), apply jumps for set bits of k; if the ancestor does not exist, print -1.
